title: Short-Distance Electric Flights Coming to Europe
paragraphs: Flying is one of the most polluting ways to travel. However, according to recent analysis, electric planes could begin carrying passengers on some short routes in Europe within the next few years.

According to the European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA), electric and hybrid planes that can fly up to 500 kilometers could cover about a quarter of Europe's existing flight routes. These include popular routes such as London to Dublin, Barcelona to Ibiza, Nice to Corsica and Athens to Santorini. Many of these routes cross water, so they cannot easily be replaced by trains.

Several companies are developing electric aircraft. Vaeridion, a German company, is building a nine-seat electric plane and hopes it will be approved to carry passengers by 2030. The company has already received commitments from airlines for 100 aircraft. Meanwhile, Aura Aero in France is developing a 19-seat hybrid-electric plane that could fly up to 1,500 kilometers. It hopes to receive certification in late 2029. According to the company, the plane could cut emissions by up to 80% and reduce operating costs by 50%. In addition, Elysian Aircraft in the Netherlands is working with the airline KLM on a 90-seat battery-electric plane that could be ready by 2035.

Electric flights are also being tested. In Scotland, the airline Loganair has agreed to buy five electric aircraft from BETA Technologies, which could make it the first European airline to use fully electric planes on scheduled flights.

However, there are still major challenges. Batteries remain heavy, which limits the size and range of electric planes. Large aircraft makers have also faced delays. For example, Airbus has recently delayed its zero-emission aircraft program.

In addition, some environmental groups point out that electric planes are only truly clean if they are charged with renewable energy. Anna Hughes of the campaign group Flight Free UK argues that people should fly less and that governments should invest in rail before electrifying flights.
Nevertheless, governments are showing support. In July 2026, the European Commission proposed extending funding for cleaner aviation to include electric aircraft.
